subject: Genetics
title: The Future of Forensic DNA
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Future of Forensic DNA.

hook.text: Future forensics won't just match DNA—they'll predict what the suspect looks like from a single cell left behind.

buildup.text: DNA phenotyping predicts eye color, hair color, skin tone, and face shape from genetic markers. It's advancing fast.

discovery.text: Parabon NanoLabs already produces 'snapshot' faces from crime scene DNA. Some have led to real identifications.

twist.text: Critics warn it could reinforce racial profiling. Predicting skin color from DNA and giving it to police is dangerous.

climax.text: Rapid DNA machines now process samples in 90 minutes at booking stations. Arrest-to-profile speed is accelerating.

punchline.text: Tomorrow's DNA tells what you look like. Not just who you are.
